html:
The global order is notably reshaped today by an intensifying trade war between the US and Canada, alongside President Trump's declared "economic warfare" on Iran and his claim that the Strait of Hormuz is now "American Territory." These actions signal a significant escalation in international economic and security tensions.

Trade & Economic Warfare: The US-Canada trade dispute has escalated dramatically, with Canada's prime minister Carney facing a "crucial test" after announcing retaliatory tariffs against 50% US tariffs on Canadian products, which Trump called a "miscalculation." Meanwhile, President Trump has declared "economic warfare" on Iran and threatened states trading with it, a move China rejects as a push for "sanctions and pressure." Iran officials dismiss the US focus on economic warfare as a sign of military failure, though Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian states it is time to end the war "in a position of strength," with other Iranian leaders sounding economic alarms. The UAE has suspended trade with Iran, a decision carrying significant costs for Tehran.

Middle East Tensions & Diplomacy: Israeli strikes near Damascus, which Syria calls a violation of international law, and extensive bombings in southern Lebanon mark continued regional instability. Turkey has issued an arrest warrant for Benjamin Netanyahu for "genocide," prompting Netanyahu to call the Turkish president an "antisemitic dictator." Iran's security chief Rezaei warned neighboring countries against joining US economic war efforts, stating Tehran would target their interests. Simultaneously, over 100 former French and British diplomats are urging their governments to impose sanctions on Israel, including bans on trade and arms sales, accusing Israel of "ethnic cleansing" and seeking to "destroy" any prospect of a Palestinian state, especially condemning Israel's E1 settlement plan.

Ukraine & European Security: Russia has begun importing fuel due to shortages caused by Ukrainian strikes on its refineries and depots. French President Emmanuel Macron announced that Paris would deliver new interceptor missiles to Ukraine after a fresh wave of Russian attacks. On Europe's eastern flank, the German army is assisting Poland in constructing a defense system along its northern and eastern borders against Russia. Internally in Ukraine, former defense minister Fedorov has decried corruption in the Defense Ministry and called for elections, adding to political pressure.

Global Health, Environment & Human Rights: The Democratic Republic of Congo is battling an "exponential" Ebola outbreak, having received over 16,000 vaccine doses, with health officials warning it could surpass the deadliest on record. Hawaii is bracing for Tropical Storm Moke, expected to bring heavy rains and strong winds just days after Hurricane Lala. Australia has recorded its first mainland mammal fatality from the spreading H5 bird flu strain, with a long-nosed fur seal dying in South Australia. A 17-year-old girl was killed in a sword attack at a school in Sweden, with an 18-year-old suspect detained.

Technology & Other Developments: A humanoid robot set a new 100-meter record of 9.39 seconds at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing. In Australia, new laws will require major tech platforms like Google and Meta to pay for publishing Australian news content. Reports suggest Iranian hackers were responsible for shutting down a power station in Britain for four days. Separately, Somali pirates are reportedly resurfacing in the seas as naval powers focus on the Persian Gulf, hijacking oil tankers. The reported casting of Meghan in Guy Ritchie’s The Gentlemen has been withdrawn due to intense backlash in the UK.
